newsitem.title: USA: Turner gains ground in merger battle - USA Today.
newsitem.headline: Turner gains ground in merger battle - USA Today.

text.p: Turner Broadcasting System Inc chairman Ted Turner is showing surprising strength in haggling with Time Warner Inc chief executive Gerald Levin over plans to merge the two companies, USA Today reported on Friday.

Turner appears to have won a key battle to keep New Line Cinema, which Levin aides said added little to Time Warner's top studio company. New Line will continue to report to Turner, not to Robert Daly, and Terry Semel of Warner Brothers.

Another potential issue is whether Time Warner might unload Turner's beloved Atlanta Braves baseball team, the Atlanta Hawks basketball team and the Goodwill Games. Some Time Warner executives consider them non-essential.
Turner is said to have raised the possibility he might personally buy at least one of the sports teams.
Levin plans to sell the $6 billion stock deal to investors in October.
Levin, Turner and an advisory committee of Time Warner and Turner executives are scrutinizing assets as they prepare to complete the merger. They met in New York on Thursday.
